summary: Fallback routing selects proxy-compat variant adding per-request translation hop causing p99 latency spike and timeouts
description:
Issue summary: During a customer traffic surge for TextFlow Labs (Dedicated, prod us-east) requests were unexpectedly routed to a 'proxy-compat' variant. That variant performs an inline translation/compatibility hop (gRPC->internal-protocol translation) which adds additional per-request latency and extra TLS handshakes, causing p99 latency to spike from ~180ms to >2.5s and producing intermittent 504 timeouts.

Impact: Customer reported steady stream of 504s and p99 latency degradations across several endpoints; user-facing feature degraded for ~2 hours during peak. Affected workloads were generation calls to redwood/gpt-6b-instr-v1 with medium context sizes.

Environment: Dedicated capacity pool for TextFlow Labs in us-east. Routing policy is default with "compat_probe" toggled on in the global routing service (recent change rolled 2026-03-04).

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Send sustained burst of generation requests at ~45 RPS to customer's pinned model in prod us-east with short prompts.
2) Observe routing decisions via /debug/routing?request_id=<id> and trace headers.
3) Confirm that a subset of requests are forwarded to a replica with variant_id starting with "proxy-compat-" by checking route tags in trace.

Observed behavior: Requests routed to proxy-compat variant include an extra network hop to the compatibility shim which performs per-request header normalization, proto translation and a short-lived TLS handshake to the on-host translator. Traces show extra 90-300ms added per request plus queueing on the translator during bursts. When translator concurrency was saturated, requests timed out with 504s.

Expected behavior: Fallback variants should be selected based on throughput/latency profiles. The incompatibility translation should be applied only for persistent long-running migrations, not as an ad-hoc fallthrough during capacity pressure.

Temporary workaround provided to customer: Set model route field fallback_policy -> "avoid-proxy-compat" or pin traffic to dedicated replicas by increasing reserved capacity. Both reduced p99 immediately.

resolution: Root cause: routing heuristic change (PR 4672) enabled compat_probe to route traffic to an inline compatibility translator ('proxy-compat') without considering translator concurrency/load. Under burst this translator became a bottleneck adding per-request translation latency and producing 504s. Actions taken: 1) Rolled back PR 4672 in production (2026-03-05) to stop automatic compat_probe selection. 2) Customer workaround: set fallback_policy to avoid-proxy-compat or increase reserved burst capacity. 3) Engineering fixes: PR 4689 introduced translator concurrency circuit breaker and adds translator_health to routing score. 4) Added integration tests for compat_probe and an entry to runbook 'fallback-routing' describing checks and mitigations. Follow-up: Monitor proxy-compat metrics for 7 days and include translator_health in canary gating for future routing changes.
